subsystems.name: Superconducting loop
subsystems.role: carries a large current to create a magnetic bubble around the spacecraft.

subsystems.name: Cryogenic and thermal system
subsystems.role: keeps the superconductor below its critical temperature and rejects heat.

subsystems.name: Plasma injection and control
subsystems.role: adds plasma to inflate the magnetic bubble to a much larger effective size.

subsystems.name: Power and energy storage
subsystems.role: energises the loop and plasma source for years in deep space.

subsystems.name: Deployable structure
subsystems.role: unfolds and holds a loop tens of kilometres across in the vacuum of space.

subsystems.name: Navigation and attitude control
subsystems.role: aims the magnetic axis into the oncoming plasma wind and steers the probe.

subsystems.name: Spacecraft bus and payload
subsystems.role: houses instruments, communications and the scientific target.

buildSteps.title: Model the plasma interaction
buildSteps.detail: Simulate how a magnetic field deflects charged particles at the speeds and densities expected in interstellar space.

buildSteps.title: Design the loop and field
buildSteps.detail: Choose a loop diameter, current and field strength that produce enough drag to slow the spacecraft over the planned distance.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the superconducting cable
buildSteps.detail: Wind superconducting tape into a cable with cooling channels, insulation and quench protection.

buildSteps.title: Build the deployable frame
buildSteps.detail: Test inflatable or mechanical booms that can unfold to full size without jamming or twisting.

buildSteps.title: Integrate on the ground
buildSteps.detail: Combine loop, cryogenics, power and plasma source in a vacuum chamber and check the magnetic bubble forms correctly.

buildSteps.title: Launch and assemble in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Send up modules and robotically connect them into one large loop, then cool it down.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate in space
buildSteps.detail: Deploy a scaled magnetic sail in the solar wind or Earth's magnetosphere and measure the force it produces.

buildSteps.title: Brake at the destination
buildSteps.detail: On approach to another star, orient the loop so the interstellar plasma strikes it head-on; adjust current to control drag.

buildSteps.title: Arrive and operate
buildSteps.detail: Once slowed, retract or stow the sail and begin the science mission.

prerequisites.why: superconductors exist, but a lightweight, cryogenic, high-current loop tens of kilometres wide has never been flown.

prerequisites.tech: In-space assembly of very large structures
prerequisites.why: space stations and solar sails have deployed, but not structures on this scale.
physicists already model how magnetic fields deflect charged particles, though interstellar conditions are poorly sampled.

prerequisites.tech: Compact nuclear power for deep space
prerequisites.why: small fission reactors have been designed and tested, but not at the power and lifetime a braking sail would need.
cooling must work for years without maintenance in deep space.
a few probes have sampled the heliosphere edge, but density, speed and magnetic fields vary and are not well mapped.

pathway.milestone: laboratory and simulation tests of magnetic sails in plasma chambers
pathway.unlocks: basic scaling laws for force versus loop size and field strength.

pathway.milestone: a small in-orbit demonstration in Earth's magnetosphere or solar wind
pathway.unlocks: measured drag and proof that a magnetic bubble can be deployed and controlled.

pathway.milestone: a heliospheric probe that changes its orbit using only a magnetic sail
an interstellar precursor probe that brakes at a nearby star
pathway.unlocks: the ability to stop at a destination instead of flying past it.

pathway.milestone: full interstellar missions with magnetic sail braking
pathway.unlocks: close-up study of other planetary systems.
